confirmed.issue: The general IBHS FORTIFIED claim-frequency/severity statistic is woven into NQR's standard storm-replacement process in a way that implies every NQR storm roof is FORTIFIED-built ('so the crew seals the deck and ring-shank-nails the cover'). The IBHS figures (cost-stats §10) describe FORTIFIED-designated homes, not NQR's standard install; presenting them as a consequence of NQR's routine cleanup step risks implying a FORTIFIED designation NQR has not claimed or verified.
confirmed.evidence: 'A FORTIFIED roof built to the IBHS standard is more than 70 percent less likely to file a claim, with damage 22 percent less severe, per the IBHS, so the crew seals the deck and ring-shank-nails the cover for wind resistance, then runs a magnet sweep for nails before leaving.'
confirmed.suggestedFix: Decouple the IBHS stat from NQR's routine step (use it as context, not as a claimed designation). Before: '…22 percent less severe, per the IBHS, so the crew seals the deck and ring-shank-nails the cover for wind resistance, then runs a magnet sweep…' After: '…22 percent less severe, per the IBHS. A Newark Quality Roofing crew installs sealed-deck and enhanced-fastening details for wind resistance where the scope calls for them, then runs a magnet sweep for nails before leaving.'
confirmed.reasoning: The offending text is present verbatim at process[2] of src/data/combo-content/livingston/storm-damage-roof-replacement.ts. The IBHS figures themselves are accurate and correctly attributed — facts-cost-stats.md §10 line 155 records "FORTIFIED homes were >70% less likely to file a claim; when they did, damage was 22% less severe ... IBHS [PRIMARY]." So this is NOT a fabricated-statistic defect. The real defect is the rhetorical coupling: the Livingston version appends a causal clause — "...22 percent less severe, per the IBHS, SO THE CREW seals the deck and ring-shank-nails the cover for wind resistance..." — that presents NQR's routine, uncertified storm install as the cause of the FORTIFIED-designation outcome. The >70%/22% figures describe homes that carry a third-party IBHS FORTIFIED designation (cost-stats §10 / sources-and-nqr-facts.md lists IBHS as authoritative for "fortified-roof STANDARDS"), not a generic sealed-deck-and-ring-shank install; the "so the crew..." link implies a FORTIFIED designation NQR has neither claimed nor verified. The committed GOLD sibling (irvington/storm-damage-roof-replacement.ts process[2], committed Combo Batch 4) uses the SAME stat but ends it cleanly as standalone resilience context — "...with damage 22% less severe, per the IBHS." — with NO "so the crew" coupling. The Livingston author diverged from gold voice. No Livingston fact, COA posture, or entity-grounding rule changes this; the fix is to decouple the stat and re-scope the install steps as NQR's own work, preserving all facts (IRC ice-barrier detail, sealed deck, ring-shank nailing, magnet sweep).
confirmed.finalFix: In src/data/combo-content/livingston/storm-damage-roof-replacement.ts process[2], replace: "A FORTIFIED roof built to the IBHS standard is more than 70 percent less likely to file a claim, with damage 22 percent less severe, per the IBHS, so the crew seals the deck and ring-shank-nails the cover for wind resistance, then runs a magnet sweep for nails before leaving." → with: "A FORTIFIED roof built to the IBHS standard is more than 70 percent less likely to file a claim, with damage 22 percent less severe, per the IBHS. A Newark Quality Roofing crew seals the deck and ring-shank-nails the cover for wind resistance where the scope calls for it, then runs a magnet sweep for nails before leaving."
